Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Intro — Pulse SDK + Redwood tracing integration (POC interest)

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking a minute to connect — I'm Emma, partnerships lead at Pulse Labs. We build a lightweight instrumentation SDK for LLM apps (request/response hooks, prompt provenance, client-side sampling) and a small team has been evaluating Redwood's tracing/export primitives.

We think there's a clean partner fit: embed Pulse SDK as an optional client-side library and wire its trace events into Redwood's tracing and prompt observability so customers get correlated traces across the client, Redwood runtime, and downstream tools.

High-level asks from our side:
- A short POC to validate trace mapping and sample rate coordination (2–3 weeks).
- Access to Redwood's tracing schema / event contract and a sandbox endpoint for test traces.
- A simple commercial path for dual-branded telemetry (co-telemetry) and an SOW once POC is green.

I've attached a one-pager that explains how the SDK works and typical event payloads (Pulse-SDK-brief.pdf). Would love to set a 30m sync next week to align on scope.

Proposed attendees: Stephanie (partnerships), Marissa (go-to-market), an engineering contact from your infra team.

Best,
Emma Chen
Partnerships Lead | Pulse Labs
emma@pulselabs.ai

Hi Emma — great to meet you (virtually) and thanks for the brief. I'm looping in Marissa from Partnerships/ISV to coordinate commercial and kickoff.

We like the approach. A couple things we need to validate before a PoC:
- Event contract: what fields will Pulse send for prompt inputs/outputs and request IDs? We try to maintain a stable trace id across the client + runtime + model call.
- Sampling controls: can you support dynamic sample rate per environment so we can lower production sampling?
- Auth/ingest: for sandbox, we prefer short-lived API keys and an ingest endpoint that accepts batched events (JSONL).

For engineering, I'm adding Vivek (infra) to this thread to confirm feasibility and propose a minimal test matrix. Marissa will own partner commercial terms.

I'm free Tue/Wed next week for a 30m sync — can you share a couple slots?

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen

On Sun, Feb 21, 2027 at 9:12 AM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Emma — great to meet you (virtually) and thanks for the brief. I'm looping in Marissa from Partnerships/ISV to coordinate commercial and kickoff.

Thanks — quick technical notes from our infra side so expectations are aligned:

1) Trace ID model: Redwood uses a 128-bit trace id (hex string) propagated in X-Redwood-Trace header; we can accept an external trace id if Pulse supplies one, but we ask for a consistent field name (trace_id) in your event payloads.

2) Event contract (minimum):
- trace_id
- span_id (optional for client hops)
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- event_type (prompt_input, prompt_output, model_call, error)
- prompt_tokens (integer)
- model_variant
- request_id (our internal request id)

3) Ingest: sandbox ingest endpoint should accept JSONL over HTTPS with an API key header (x-pulse-api-key). Support for batch sizes up to 500 events is fine.

4) Sampling: we can expose a sample_rate header in the POC that instructs the SDK to reduce client-side sampling; we will also provide a small control plane endpoint for toggling rates by environment.

5) Security: for the PoC we prefer shared sandbox keys and no PII in events; if you need PII we need a signed DPIA and scoping.

Proposed PoC matrix (2 weeks):
- Week 1: wire simple client demo (instrumented web UI) -> Pulse SDK sends events to Redwood sandbox; validate trace join and event mapping.
- Week 2: scale test (100 req/s synthetic traffic), sampling behavior, and generate sample dashboards.

If that looks good we'll draft a scoped SOW and a timeline.

—Vivek
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

On Mon, Feb 22, 2027 at 11:03 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks — quick technical notes from our infra side so expectations are aligned:

Thanks Vivek, this is helpful and aligns with what we built. A few quick clarifications from Pulse: 

- We currently provide trace_id and span_id in the SDK and can emit event_type exactly as you described. We also attach a client_session_id that may be useful for client-only correlation.
- We can ship a sandbox ingest endpoint that accepts JSONL + x-pulse-api-key. We've attached a draft SOW that scopes the PoC and an initial architecture diagram for the proposed flow (Pulse-Redwood-SOW-draft.pdf, pulse-redwood-arch-diagram.png).
- On PII: we can redact headers and fields for the PoC; flagship customers sometimes do include user identifiers but we'll follow Redwood's policy for sandbox work.

Proposed PoC timeline:
- Kickoff: Mon 1 Mar 2027
- Week 1: Instrument demo client + validate trace joins
- Week 2: Load test, dashboarding, and review

We also included a short commercial note: if PoC is successful, Pulse recommends a co-marketing credit and a referral revenue share for mutual customers — happy to discuss with Marissa during commercial review.

Looking forward — Rajiv
Eng + Partnerships | Pulse Labs
